title: Old queued completion replays over a newer one
story: An offline completion is replayed over a newer live one. The fix drops the queued copy after a live send. Later it deleted a real queued completion when the live send was a blank form.
entry: Mobile outbox defect. A completion queued offline is replayed over a newer live send under the same stable id. Fix: after a successful live send, remove the queued item. Payments and notes use unique ids, so they never collide.
steps: Later tasks are features. The race is not a problem the model has. Only CLAUDE.md's always-loaded known-defect note names it.
No error, so no lookup after failure. The diff check matches named handles on changed lines, and an outbox edit warns.
The diff check is mechanical. The model does not choose the words.
Two entries look like one problem: 'stale write over newer send: fixed' and 'same id, concurrent flush: open'. The fixed one reads as the answer to the open one.
One warning line per entry in the main session and the decisions journal. The Opus reviewer rules.
The only stored fix is a rule: on live success, drop the queued copy. That later deleted the queued real completion. Adapting it to a new stable-id kind copies the door.
A race's footprint is identical in a good and a bad run. No test encodes the race. The old Jest case passes even on trees where its rule destroys a bill.
Nothing fails in a session. In the field the winner is whichever request the server finishes last. Nothing climbs. The finder was code reading.
Written at solve time, it is stored with 'never collide' true and the deletion unseen. The race has a diagnosis but no fix, so it is a candidate only.
The entry stayed true by its own test while a later fix found it was a door through screens outside its footprint.

title: Dispatcher flip sends the whole history
when: Entry from 2026-08-01 review; ship plan later
source: Commit c731e66; migration 0046; HANDOFF lines 157-166; SHIP-PLAN line 102
story: Nothing fails until FIXFLOW_ENABLE_DISPATCHER is switched on. Then an unseeded cursor drains 87 events as live WhatsApp messages, 36 of them triggers. Later tasks are a drain audit and a host move.
entry: Trap, operator action. With no cursor row, run_dispatch_once starts at last_seq=0 and drains all of job_event as live messages. Measured on prod: 87 events, 36 triggers. Fix: migration 0046 seeds the cursor at the latest seq. A 2-day age skip covers a hand reset.
steps: Later tasks are a drain audit and a host move. Neither is 'a dispatcher problem'. The hazard is a state the next operator action meets.
No error exists. The design reaches operator hazards only through the action wording. The diff check cannot see state outside git, such as an env flip or database rows.
The entry's action is 'enable dispatcher'. Later sessions act as drain, restore, re-point or close the window. A hit depends on guessing those verbs.
At best a candidate. Entries about prod data are capped at candidate until a probe and an age-guard test exist.
The main session gets one card.
The stored fix, seed at head, with the age guard covering the rest, fails the new state. Events pile up above the July seed while OFF, and months-old writes count as fresh.
The probe runs on a throwaway database migrated to head. It cannot count events above the prod cursor. The 36 came from a prod query.
The failure would be real customer messages, seen in no session. What must go up is a prod query result, which an operator runs, not a model.
Write-then-approve by a different Opus matched what happened. The review fixed the dead-letter guard, the downgrade and a test that pinned the consent leak before merge.
'Enabling is forward-only' decays with prod rows that no footprint item sees. The entry stays validated. The ship plan, not the store, carries the live rule.

title: Clinic check stalls with no test named
story: A parallel check ends 'no test made progress for 600s'. The cause is unknown. The related entry from a faster-check session covers a different cause, a crashed worker, and the rerun passed with no fix.
entry: No entry from the 9 Nov stall. The related entry: parallel pass ends 'no test made progress for 600s' after a worker died. Under pytest-xdist loadfile the run hangs. Under load the crash is reported at once. Set DIST_MODE to 'load'.
steps: Sonnet was measuring runs mid-task. The log tail, with dots to 96 %, 'exit 1, 961.0s' and the watchdog line, was in the window.
A cheap agent that hits an unexpected gate error looks it up before retrying.
The query is the watchdog line. What may matter is not in it. The watchdog reports no test id. Low free memory and load sit only in load samples.
An exact template hit on the 11-05 entry, a different cause. No worker died and the mode is already 'load'. The ambiguity flag needs more than one recorded cause.
Nothing to adapt. The entry only rules out one cause. The model then does what it did without a library: rerun once more.
The gate's 'not applies' is right. But the only verdict on the failure is the rerun. It passed with no fix, so 'resolved' is recorded for nothing.
Escalating hands up the same silence: dots, one watchdog line, no test id, no stack, machine state gone. A higher model gets no more evidence.
Nothing is solved, so nothing is written. The next stall starts from zero.
The 11-05 entry stays validated and matches every stall's exact line. Each non-crash stall pays a lookup and a 'not applies'.

title: Flaky clinic tests read random tags as figures
story: Attack tests fail by chance because a number helper reads record ids, a CSRF token and random hex tags as money figures. Three writers made three fixes in about 7 hours. One mask hides real figures.
entry: Flaky test, clinic withholding tests. S09/S07 attack tests fail by chance: a difference of two numbers on a page equals a hidden amount. numbers() reads ids, CSRF token and random hex tags as figures. Fix: strip those; a unit test pins what is read and ignored.
steps: Sonnet was in a faster-check session. The task is speed. The failing assertion is in the run log.
An unexpected gate error is looked up before retry.
The canonicaliser masks hex runs, ids and free numbers. The coincidence of a figure with a hex tag is the only clue, and masking removes it. The match must come from the test id.
At 23:49 UTC the test frame hits the root's entry. At 23:00, in a file outside its footprint, a miss is likely.
The main Sonnet session gets a candidate card with a summary and unverified negatives, no fix. The branch lacks the fix commit.
The summary gives the cause, not the fix. The root's fix is half right: a review found its mask 'would hide SYN Till 654321 moved'. Adapting it spreads a mask that hides real figures.
A planted-tag unit test makes the chance repeatable, so a control pair can flip. It proves the condition, not today's cause. The session's own check of its wrong idea was 'tests passing'.
A second Opus review caught the wrong sequence guess. The same review approved a retry delay that was still over the race window.
Three writers made three fixes for one cause in about 7 hours. 'Store when solved' stores the 00:06 UTC one. The write trigger likely skips the root's routine fix.
In-project, a later test fails at merge naming random_tag, so the entry becomes redundant. Cross-project, FixFlow's backend has no Hypothesis and no uuid4().hex labels.

title: Two pytest runs deadlock on one test database
story: 22 integration tests failed together with no code change. A lone rerun passed. Two pytest processes, from different sessions, shared one test database and deadlocked on its schema setup.
entry: Trap, FixFlow backend tests. Many integration tests fail together (22 in one run) with no code change; a rerun alone passes. Two pytest processes ran against one test database. Never run two pytest processes against that database at once.
steps: In FixFlow, a test run with 22 red tests puts the failure in the window.
An unexpected gate error is looked up before retry.
22 failures carry 22 test ids and lock errors. The deciding fact, a second pytest process from another session, is in no log the failing session holds.
A deadlock template has many causes. An ambiguous template never makes a lead alone. At best a candidate. In the clinic, a word match returns a rule with a different mechanism.
In FixFlow the runner is often a subagent in a worktree. Its window starts empty and cannot see the sibling agent holding the lock.
The fix is a rule about other sessions. The failing agent cannot stop the other process. It can only rerun alone.
Process state at the moment of failure is gone once the other process exits. No check, no control pair.
It was traced once. The cost of that trace is recorded nowhere and the session is gone.
HANDOFF traps are seeded as trap entries. A one-line rule is cheap and true in FixFlow.
In the clinic, 'never two at once' contradicts the designed two slots and misses its mechanism, which is a database drop. The other design is FixFlow-only and does not specify cross-project use.

title: Clinic socket refusal retry and its timing
when: Commits dd74a3d and 030c6cb; reviews over several hours
source: Commits dd74a3d, 030c6cb; round2.md line 8; task.md lines 105, 344
story: A race test failed 2 of 22 runs with 'No buffer space available' on loopback. A retry of 0.05 s per attempt was added. Reviews later found its total delay could make a call look blocked.
entry: Gate flake, clinic check on Windows. The serial race pass fails with 'No buffer space available (10055)' on loopback connect. connect_retry retries psycopg.connect up to 6 times for that message only. Delay is 0.05 s per attempt, under the race window's 0.6 s.
steps: A full-check log with a refused connect in a race test is in the window.
An unexpected gate error is looked up before retry.
The error line is exact and distinctive.
Exact template, one recorded cause: a clean hit.
Copying the retry copies a hidden coupling: its total delay against another test's timing window. The entry's words and footprint do not name that coupling.
The retry's unit tests pass. The safety claim had no test until later. The race tests it protects passed under load with a broken lock. A green check certified the wrong property.

Sonnet wrote the claim. An Opus review found one problem and approved 0.05 s per attempt, 0.75 s in total. The Fable root caught it at the gate. Every rung paid, and the middle one endorsed a wrong fix.
Written at solve time, the entry stores the record's false sentence that a retry cannot make a call look blocked.
It was fixed in place within hours. An entry from 030c6cb must be superseded, which needs an Opus actor and a second Opus approver.
